title: Performance management
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:32Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: No point in the bank covers performance management of staff; monitoring performance compares business results with the plan, which is a different idea from setting goals and giving feedback to employees.

draft.title: Performance management
card: Performance management is the ongoing process a business uses to get the best work from its staff. It links each worker's efforts to the goals of the business.
It has three steps. Goals are set with the worker. Their work is reviewed against those goals. Feedback is then given on what went well and what to improve.
the aim is to help the worker grow. Feedback is used to find strengths, gaps in skills and the support the worker needs.
the aim is to judge the worker. Review results are used to make decisions on pay, promotion or other changes to the job.
draft.remember: Set goals, review work, give feedback, then use the results to develop staff or to decide pay and promotion.

a.q: Which step of performance management is a manager carrying out when she compares a worker's results with the goals agreed earlier?
a.why: Comparing results with agreed goals is the review step. Giving feedback is different: it is telling the worker what the review found and how to improve.
a.clue: The goals already exist. What is being checked against them?

b.q: Dev runs a bakery in Wagga Wagga. After each review, he uses the results to choose which bakers receive a pay rise. What is the aim of his performance management?
opts: Developmental, because goals were set first
b.why: Using review results to decide pay is the evaluative aim. Feedback and goal setting also happen in developmental systems, so they do not show which aim is being used. The regular timing of reviews does not show the aim either.
b.clue: Look at what the results are used for, not at the steps.
